reasoning: The core problem—whether evaluation presentation STRUCTURE (independent of item content) leaks the eval-frame and shifts refusal behavior and verbalized test-belief—is heavily covered by 2025-2026 work. "Is Evaluation Awareness Just Format Sensitivity?" (arXiv 2603.19426) uses a controlled 2x2 design varying format while holding content constant and finds probes track benchmark-canonical structure rather than context; "Verbalized Eval Awareness Inflates Measured Safety" (Goodfire/LessWrong) measures both verbalized eval-belief and refusal-rate shifts (3-18 pp, causal) on open models (Qwen 3, OLMo 3, Kimi); "Probe-Rewrite-Evaluate" (2509.00591) rewrites test-like into deploy-like/conversational prompts and measures refusal/honesty shifts; and the eval-awareness community already names batching/"convenient packaging" and "unnaturally clean arc" as recognized structural cues. The precise operationalization (batching identical items back-to-back vs. interleaving them in a natural conversation, single small open model, paired per-item stats on refusal + 0-100% verbalized test-belief) is a narrow instantiation not found verbatim, but the problem and nearly all of the proposed measurements/manipulations are already established, leaving only a minor confirmatory gap.

evidence.title: Is Evaluation Awareness Just Format Sensitivity? Limitations of Probe-Based Evidence under Controlled Prompt Structure
evidence.summary: Uses a controlled 2x2 dataset and diagnostic rewrites that vary prompt format while holding content stable; finds eval-awareness signals primarily track benchmark-canonical STRUCTURE and fail to generalize to free-form/conversational prompts. Directly addresses whether structure (not content) drives the eval-frame effect.

evidence.title: Verbalized Eval Awareness Inflates Measured Safety
evidence.summary: Across 19 benchmarks and 8 models (incl. open: Qwen 3 0.6B-32B, OLMo 3, Kimi), measures verbalized eval-awareness and shows models refuse 3-18 pp more when they verbalize test-belief; causal injection/removal experiments confirm eval-awareness increases refusal. Covers the proposal's refusal + verbalized-test-belief measurements.

evidence.title: Probe-Rewrite-Evaluate: A Workflow for Reliable Benchmarks and Quantifying Evaluation Awareness
evidence.summary: Rewrites prompts from test-like to deploy-like (more conversational) and measures statistically significant behavioral shifts: +12.8% refusals, +12.6% honesty, -25% deception, scaling with model size. Covers the conversational-vs-benchmark contrast and paired behavioral measurement.

evidence.title: Do LLMs Know They Are Being Tested? Evaluation Awareness and Incentive-Sensitive Failures in GPT-OSS-20B
evidence.summary: Studies evaluation awareness and behavioral (incl. refusal) shifts on a single small open model (GPT-OSS-20B), closely matching the proposal's single-small-open-model, inference-only setup.

evidence.title: Where we are on evaluation awareness
evidence.summary: Community survey naming structural cues that leak the eval-frame: 'convenient information packaging', 'unnaturally clean arc from setup to decision point', and chat-vs-agentic differences—indicating batching/packaging is already a recognized structural cue.
